title: The Field Nobody Wanted
subtitle: 自然生态 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 自然生态（自然生态·自然与荒野）
meta: 主题语境：自然生态（自然生态·自然与荒野）　|　核心词汇：nature　|　正文 382 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 nature 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: Nature, my father said, is a word for the bits nobody has got round to. Behind the last house in our village there is a field that nobody farmed, fenced or wanted, and for eleven years it was the best ① nature any of us had access to. Nature, in a village like ours, is whatever is left over. It was not wild in any romantic sense; it was a ② nature of docks, nettles and scrap, and it taught me more than the reserve six miles away, which was managed, signposted and dull; nature, in a place like that, is only what the sign says.

My father, who was a careful man, disapproved of the word. 'Nature,' he said, 'is what people call the bits they have not got round to.' He had a point, and I have spent years deciding how much of one. The ③ nature of the field was that it had been worked hard and then abandoned, and everything in it was a consequence of that, not of ④ nature being generous.

What I noticed, at about ten, was that the field changed faster than the reserve. By ⑤ nature it should have gone to scrub and stayed there; instead it went to scrub, burned, went to grass, was cut for hay by a man with no permission, and came back different every year. Stability, I now think, is the thing people admire in ⑥ nature and the thing it has least of.

In 2009 the field was bought, fenced and planted with eleven hundred saplings, which is what happens when somebody decides a place is ⑦ natural. Half of them died in the first drought and the rest are doing well, and ⑧ by nature I am on the side of the trees and against myself, because I know exactly what was lost and I still think it was worth it.

I am a teacher now and I take children to the reserve, because that is what teachers do. What I would rather do is take them to a field nobody wants and ask them what is ⑨ natural about it. Nothing, is the answer, and everything: the docks came from a farm, the scrap came from a war, and the ⑩ nature of the place is simply that nobody has edited it for eleven years.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 大自然；自然界（总称）
B. n. 本性；天性；本质（the nature of）
C. n. 性质；种类（of this nature）
D. adj. 自然的；天然的（natural）
E. 固定搭配：by nature 天生；本性上
F. 固定搭配：in nature 实际上；本质上（用于强调）
G. n. （某地的）自然环境；景物
H. n. 本来的样子；未经修饰的状态

items.q: the best nature any of us had access to
it was a nature of docks, nettles and scrap
The nature of the field was that it had been worked hard and then abandoned
By nature it should have gone to scrub
the thing people admire in nature
when somebody decides a place is natural
by nature I am on the side of the trees
ask them what is natural about it
the nature of the place is simply that nobody has edited it

answers.why: 指我们唯一能接触到的“自然环境、野地”，说那块地是村里最好的一片自然。
a nature of ... 指“……这样一种性质／类型”，说它是由酸模、荨麻和废铁构成的那种自然。
the nature of 意为“……的本质、本来面目”，说这块地的实质是被精耕后又被抛弃。
指大自然本身，说一切都是那种历史的后果，而不是自然的慷慨。
by nature 此处意为“按道理、本质上说”，说按常理它该变成灌木丛并不再变化。
指“大自然”，说稳定性恰恰是人们在自然里最不具备的东西。
natural 作形容词，意为“天然的、自然的”，说有人认定这地方够天然便种上树苗。
by nature 意为“天生、本性上”，说我本性站在树的一边而反对自己。
同样作形容词，问孩子们觉得这块地哪里算“天然的”。
指“本来的样子、未经编辑的状态”，说这地方的本质就是十一年没人去修饰它。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 十一年里，那是我们唯一能接触到的自然环境。（nature）
这块地的本质是：被精耕过，然后被抛弃。（the nature of）
按常理它该变成灌木丛并不再变化。（by nature）
稳定性恰恰是自然最不具备的东西。（nature）
有人认定这地方够天然，于是种上一千一百棵树苗。（natural）
我本性站在树的一边，却反对自己。（by nature）
answers: For eleven years it was the only piece of nature any of us had access to.
The nature of the field was that it had been worked hard and then abandoned.
By nature it should have gone to scrub and stayed there.
Stability is the thing people admire in nature and the thing it has least of.
Somebody decided the place was natural and planted eleven hundred saplings.
By nature I am on the side of the trees and against myself.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 nature 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: For eleven years the unwanted field was the best nature any of us had access to.
It was not wild in any romantic sense; it was a nature of docks, nettles and scrap.
The nature of the field was that it had been worked hard and then abandoned.
By nature it should have gone to scrub and stayed there, but it changed every year.
Somebody decided the place was natural and planted eleven hundred saplings, half of which died.
The nature of the place is simply that nobody has edited it for eleven years.
